SYNTHETIC FIXTURE - SKL-242 - not real data
Story: validated ledger totals (synthetic story for the dossier-size fixture)

As a bookkeeper reading a ledger batch, I want every ledger part to refuse malformed and negative
entries and to report the entries over a limit, so a typo cannot silently change a total.

Acceptance criteria

1. Parsing. Each ledger part reads a line as `name,amount`, with surrounding whitespace removed
   from both fields. A line with no separator, more than one separator, an empty name, or an amount
   that is not a non-negative whole number raises the part's entry error, and the message names the
   part and the offending text.
2. Skipped lines. Blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `#` are skipped, not
   parsed, by every function that reads a batch.
3. Line numbers. An entry error raised while reading a batch names the one-based number of the
   offending line in the batch as given, counting skipped lines.
4. Totals. The total is the sum of the amounts of the parsed entries; an empty batch totals zero.
5. Largest. The largest entry is the one with the greatest amount, ties broken by the greater name;
   an empty batch has no largest entry.
6. Over the limit. Entries whose amount is strictly greater than the limit are returned as
   `(name, amount)` pairs in batch order. The limit defaults to 250 and can be passed per call.
7. Summary. The summary names the part, the entry count, the total, the limit and the names of the
   entries over it, or `none` when no entry is over it.
8. Average. The average is the whole-number mean of the amounts; an empty batch raises the part's
   entry error instead of returning zero.
9. Names. The names are returned once each, in the order they first appear.
10. Report. The report lists every entry sorted by name, then amount, with the names padded to the
    longest name, the amounts right-aligned in eight columns, an `over` flag on the entries over
    the limit, and the summary as its last line, ending in a newline.
11. Separator. Every function takes an optional separator, defaulting to a comma, and passes it on
    to the parser.

Out of scope

- Currency, decimal amounts and thousands separators.
- Reading batches from files or streams; every function takes a list of lines.
- Persisting totals or reports.

Notes for reviewers

- The change is the same in all twenty-five ledger parts, so a defect in one part is a defect in
  every part; report it once with the list of parts it affects.
- The base version accepted negative amounts and summed comment lines; both are the defects this
  story fixes, not behaviour to preserve.
- There is no test suite for the ledger parts in this repository; a finding about missing tests is
  in scope.
